findings.evidence: Lines 133–154 define the homomorphism solely to feed `MulEquiv.ofBijective` at line 163; the public equivalence already provides `.toMonoidHom`.
findings.fix: Make both helpers private and retain `equalizerPointsEquiv` as the public isomorphism.
findings.issue: `equalizerPointsHom` and `equalizerPointsHom_bijective` expose an implementation layer duplicated by the canonical `equalizerPointsEquiv` and its coercion lemma.

findings.evidence: The explicit `[simp]` coercion/factorization lemmas provide forward and inverse behavior, while lines 160, 188, and 228 expose the `MulEquiv.ofBijective`, composition, and `subgroupCongr` implementations.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]`; prove the computation lemmas with `:= (rfl)` or internally unfold the definitions so downstream users rely on the API rather than representation bodies.
findings.issue: All three public constructions `equalizerPointsEquiv`, `liftEqualizerPoints`, and `fixedPointsEquiv` carry `@[expose]` even though their public behavior is already characterized by lemmas at lines 166–179, 197–211, and 235–239.

findings.evidence: The lemmas at lines 103–112 and 217–221 orient subgroup membership to pointwise propositions and terminate in the existing `AlgHom.mem_equalizer` normal form.
findings.issue: The characteristic membership criteria `mem_eqLocus_mapValue_iff` and `mem_eqLocus_mapValue_id_iff` are not tagged `@[simp]`, so simplification cannot reduce membership in these newly defined equalizer/fixed-point subgroups to pointwise equations.

summary: The canonical constructions have usable computation lemmas, but their bodies are unnecessarily exposed and an implementation-only homomorphism is public.
